sm: The host explains why men stopped wearing suspenders. He first notes that before belts and suspenders, men used drawstrings, medieval girdles, codpieces and sashes, so choosing how to hold up pants has always been a matter of fashion. Suspenders date to 1736 in France, spread with the rise of breeches, and peaked in the Victorian era as hidden underwear that everyone owned. Belts were mostly utility items until World War I, when fabric shortages led to lower-rise trousers. Returning soldiers and Hollywood stars popularized belts and belt loops, so belt sales matched suspender sales by the late 1930s. Suspenders had a brief revival in the 1980s Wall Street look, then fell again. He concludes that modern trousers have lower waistlines and belt loops and are not made for suspenders, and that casual fashion made them seem old-fashioned.
